title: Choosing the right repeat — all together
idea: MEET. Wrap-up: given a problem, name the shape (for/while), the repeated step, what you keep (counter/accumulator), and whether break/continue is needed. Review-leaning. No code.

exercises.prompt: 'Add up the numbers 1 to 50.' Shape and what you keep?
exercises.explanation: 1 to 50 is a known count (for), and summing values needs an accumulator (running total).

exercises.prompt: 'Keep asking for a number until they type 0, then say how many you got.' Shape and what you keep?
exercises.explanation: Stopping when they type 0 is a condition (while), and 'how many you got' needs a counter.

exercises.prompt: 'Print 1 to 100 but stop at the first multiple of 7.' Shape and extra tool?
options: for (known range) + break (stop at first match)
exercises.explanation: The range 1 to 100 is known (for), and 'stop at the first' means break.

exercises.prompt: 'Print 1 to 20 but skip the multiples of 5.' Shape and extra tool?
exercises.explanation: 1 to 20 is a known range (for); skipping some passes is continue.

exercises.prompt: Match each problem to its loop shape.
exercises.explanation: Known counts (count down 10, 5 guests) are for; stopping on a condition (below 1, 'yes') is while.

exercises.prompt: Select ALL problems that need a COUNTER.
options: How many numbers 1 to 30 are even
exercises.explanation: Counting HOW MANY (even numbers, yeses) uses a counter. Sums and totals use an accumulator.

exercises.prompt: Select ALL problems that need an ACCUMULATOR.
exercises.explanation: Building a SUM (of 1 to 10, of prices) uses an accumulator. Counting how many uses a counter.

exercises.prompt: A single problem can need a for loop, a counter, AND an if inside the loop together.
exercises.explanation: True. 'Count how many of 1 to 50 are even' uses a for loop, a counter, and an if — tools combine.

exercises.prompt: Order the planning questions for ANY repetition problem.
blocks: Is the count known (for) or does it stop on a condition (while)?
What single step repeats each pass?
Do I keep a counter or accumulator, and do I need if / break / continue?
exercises.explanation: Pick the shape, name the repeated step, then decide the state and any break/continue. That is the whole plan.

exercises.prompt: What did this unit teach you to do BEFORE writing any loop?
options: Choose the right kind of repeat and plan its parts
exercises.explanation: You learned to read a problem and pick the loop shape and tools first — the plan comes before the code.
